title: Customers who never ordered (anti-join)
problem_md:
Marketing wants to send a first-order coupon to people who created an account but **never placed an order on
any channel**. Some marketplace orders are guest checkouts, so `orders.customer_id` can be `NULL`.

```sql
CREATE TABLE customers (
  customer_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
  name        TEXT NOT NULL,
  city        TEXT
);

CREATE TABLE orders (
  order_id    INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
  customer_id INTEGER,          -- NULL for guest checkouts
  channel     TEXT NOT NULL,
  order_date  TEXT NOT NULL
);
```

**Task.** Return `customer_id` and `name` of every customer with **no rows** in `orders`.
Order by `customer_id`.

examples.input: customers 1..6; orders exist for customers 1, 3, 5 and one guest order with customer_id NULL
examples.output:
customer_id | name
2           | Diya Sharma
4           | Ananya Iyer
6           | Meera Nair

hints: Start from `customers` and keep customers even when there is no matching order.
A `LEFT JOIN` produces NULLs on the orders side when there is no match - filter for those.
`... LEFT JOIN orders o ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id WHERE o.order_id IS NULL`. Be careful: `NOT IN (SELECT customer_id FROM orders)` returns nothing here - why?
starter_code:
-- Write your query here
SELECT c.customer_id, c.name
FROM customers c
solution_code:
SELECT c.customer_id, c.name
FROM customers c
LEFT JOIN orders o ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id
WHERE o.order_id IS NULL
ORDER BY c.customer_id;
solution_md:
**Anti-join pattern.** "Rows in A with no match in B" is an *anti-join*. Two idiomatic forms:

```sql
-- 1) LEFT JOIN ... IS NULL
SELECT c.customer_id, c.name
FROM customers c
LEFT JOIN orders o ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id
WHERE o.order_id IS NULL;            -- test a NOT NULL column of the right table

-- 2) NOT EXISTS (often the clearest, same plan in PostgreSQL)
SELECT c.customer_id, c.name
FROM customers c
WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM orders o WHERE o.customer_id = c.customer_id);
```

PostgreSQL plans both as a *Hash Anti Join*.

**The `NOT IN` trap.** `WHERE c.customer_id NOT IN (SELECT customer_id FROM orders)` returns **zero rows** here,
because the subquery contains a `NULL` (the guest order). `x NOT IN (1, 3, NULL)` means
`x <> 1 AND x <> 3 AND x <> NULL`, and `x <> NULL` is `UNKNOWN`, so the whole predicate is never `TRUE`.
Prefer `NOT EXISTS`, or add `WHERE customer_id IS NOT NULL` inside the subquery.

**Index.** An index on `orders (customer_id)` lets the anti-join probe orders per customer instead of scanning;
for this one-off report a hash anti-join over a full scan is also fine.
